'''Jeremy O'Brien''' (born 1975, Australia<ref>{{cite book|last=Barrow|first=John D.|title=Science and ultimate reality: quantum theory, cosmology, and complexity|year=2004|publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]]|isbn=978-0-521-83113-0|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=K_OfC0Pte_8C&pg=PA695|author-link=John D. Barrow |author2=Davies, Paul C. W. |author2-link=Paul C. W. Davies |author3=Harper, Charles L. |page=695}}</ref>) is a  physicist who researches in [[quantum optics]], optical [[quantum metrology]] and [[quantum information science]].<ref name="opn">{{cite news|title=2010 OSA Awards |url=http://www.osa.org/awards_and_grants/Awards/42-OSAAwards_june_v2.pdf |access-date=29 May 2010 |newspaper=Optics and Photonics News |date=June 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100612210105/http://osa.org/awards_and_grants/Awards/42-OSAAwards_june_v2.pdf |archive-date=12 June 2010 }}</ref> He co-founded and is [[Chief executive officer|CEO]] of the quantum computing firm [[PsiQuantum]].<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite news|last=Titcomb|first=James|date=2021-07-27|title=Quantum computing start-up founded by British academics worth $3.2bn|language=en-GB|work=The Telegraph|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/technology/2021/07/27/quantum-computing-start-up-founded-british-academics-worth-32bn/|access-date=2021-07-27|issn=0307-1235}}</ref> Formerly, he was Professorial [[Research Fellow]] in Physics and Electrical Engineering at the [[University of Bristol]], and director of its Centre for Quantum Photonics.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bristol University Physics—Centre for Quantum Photonics—Academic Staff|url=http://www.phy.bris.ac.uk/groups/cqp/people.php|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100208160740/http://www.phy.bris.ac.uk/groups/cqp/people.php|archive-date=8 February 2010|publisher=University of Bristol|access-date=29 May 2010}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite news|last=Titcomb|first=James|date=2019-11-16|title=Bristol professor's secretive quantum computing start-up raises £179m|language=en-GB|work=The Telegraph|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/technology/2019/11/16/bristol-professors-secretive-quantum-computing-start-up-raises/|access-date=2021-07-27|issn=0307-1235}}</ref>

His work in optical [[quantum computing]] has included the demonstration of the first optical quantum [[controlled NOT gate]].<ref name="nature2003">{{cite journal|last=O'Brien|first=JL|author2=Pryde, GJ |author3=White, AG |author4=Ralph, TC |author5= Branning, D |title=Demonstration of an all-optical quantum controlled-NOT gate|journal=Nature| year=2003|volume=426|issue=6964|pages=264–267|doi=10.1038/nature02054|pmid=14628045 |arxiv = quant-ph/0403062 |bibcode = 2003Natur.426..264O |s2cid=9883628}}</ref>

==Honours and awards==
*2009 European Quantum Information Young Investigator Award<ref>{{cite web|title=QIPC Young Investigator Award 2009 |url=http://www.qurope.net/Q_Confs/q_confs.php?type=confs&trig_id=6 |publisher=QUROPE (Quantum Information Processing and Communication in Europe) |access-date=29 May 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100916084158/http://www.qurope.net/Q_Confs/q_confs.php?type=confs&trig_id=6 |archive-date=16 September 2010 }}</ref>
*2010 [[Adolph Lomb Medal]] of the [[Optical Society of America]]<ref name="opn"/>
*2010 [[IUPAP]] Prize in Atomic Molecular and Optical Physics<ref>{{cite web|title=Double honour for Professor O'Brien|url=http://bristol.ac.uk/news/2010/7040.html|publisher=[[University of Bristol]]|access-date=29 May 2010}}</ref>
*2010 Moseley medal and prize of the [[Institute of Physics]]<ref>{{cite web|title=2010 Moseley medal and prize|url=http://www.iop.org/about/awards/career/moseley/medallists/page_43973.html|publisher=Institute of Physics|access-date=5 July 2010}}</ref>
*2010 [[Daiwa Adrian Prize]]
*2011 Elected to the [[Global Young Academy]] {{cite web|title=PsiQuantum Valuation|url=https://www.eutechfuture.com/innovation/psiquantum-valuation-a-deep-dive-into-the-quantum-computing-pioneer/|access-date=25 September 2025}}
